Definition: from G1537 and G2827; to deviate, i.e. (absolutely) to shun (literally or figuratively), or (relatively) to decline (from piety):--avoid, eschew, go out of the way.
BiblicalUsage: To turn aside is to deviate from the road, and the Bible uses it for the whole human race and for the Christian's duty. Paul says they are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable, and he tells the Romans to mark those who cause divisions and avoid them. Peter says to let him eschew evil and do good, to seek peace and ensue it, because the same word that describes the fall also describes the escape from it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe turning aside is the story of every heart, because we all go out of the way, and turning back is the story of grace. I hold that avoiding evil is not fear but wisdom, and seeking peace is not weakness but strength.
